claim: For the two-player binary extraction game with payoff \(u_i(h_i,h_j)=b h_i-L\Pr(\Theta_t\le h_i+h_j)\), \(L>0\), \(b/L=19/50\), and threshold law \((\Pr(\Theta_t=1),\Pr(\Theta_t=2),\Pr(\Theta_t=3),\Pr(\Theta_t=4))=(2/5-t,1/10+3t,3/10-3t,1/5+t)\) for \(0\le t\le1/10\), every law has mean \(23/10\) and variance \(141/100\), yet the game is coordination for \(0\le t<1/50\), a strict Prisoner’s Dilemma for \(1/50<t<7/75\), and anti-coordination for \(7/75<t\le1/10\), with best-response ties at the two boundary values.
integrity_notes: The proof uses exact algebra and rational parameters; a standalone exact-arithmetic checker is included.
Independent audit and independent validation have not been performed.
scientific_limitations: Static two-player binary-action game with risk-neutral expected payoffs and a common threshold.
No empirical behavior, repeated extraction, heterogeneity, learning, enforcement, or resource recovery is modeled.
The closest 2017 source was available only as an abstract and metadata during this review, leaving a residual novelty risk.
title: Moment-matched thresholds switch a binary resource game across three equilibrium regimes
